matchingRules.priority: Preserve existing seven q.year values. Reviewed rules override conflicting source-title dates. Blocked contexts never receive reviewed original dates.
matchingRules.citationOnly: Work titles found only in citations require manual review; do not blindly match all historical mentions.
matchingRules.dateMeaning: Bounds date the work, textual formation, or first performance, not necessarily a first utterance or modern English wording. Negative values mean BCE; no year zero. Uncertainty labels are mandatory.
matchingRules.multipleMatches: Retain unknown if conflicting work matches remain.
matchingRules.representedSpeakers: An attributed speaker can differ from the work author. Explicit Plato dialogue contexts under Socrates are supported; never infer a work from a speaker lifetime.

mappings.label: c. 2000–1800 BCE (Middle Kingdom composition)
mappings.basis: UCL assigns composition to Dynasty 12; rounded Met chronology distinguishes this from the fictional Old Kingdom setting.
mappings.note: Override source title c. 2350 BC. Rounded dynasty envelope c. 2000–1800 BCE is not an exact scholarly composition bound.

mappings.label: 23rd–18th century BCE (disputed)
mappings.basis: Helle allows Old Akkadian authorship or later composition; most manuscripts are eighteenth-century. Bounds are an uncertainty envelope, not a lifetime date.
mappings.note: Traditional twenty-third-century attribution versus eighteenth-century witnesses; disputed authorship. Do not label 2300 BCE independently established.
observedContexts: A Hymn to Inana (23rd century BCE)

mappings.label: c. 700 BCE
mappings.basis: Cambridge classical-source chronology dates Works and Days approximately 700 BCE.

mappings.label: c. 800–650 BCE
mappings.basis: Chicago Library gives eighth to mid-seventh century composition, allowing earlier traditions; writing-down and manuscript dates differ.
mappings.note: Lower bound is conventional, not a proven earliest oral origin. Translations-only contexts cannot receive this date.

mappings.label: c. 171–175 CE
mappings.basis: IEP dates the campaign notebook probably 171–175 CE; Book I may be separate.
mappings.note: Override source c. AD 121–180, the author lifetime. Exact notebook chronology remains uncertain.

mappings.label: c. 108 CE (teaching recorded by Arrian)
mappings.basis: SEP places the represented teaching around 108 CE; Arrian records it. This is not an exact publication date.
mappings.note: Ancient recorded teaching; do not extend to Golden Sayings or generic community quotes.

mappings.label: c. 135 CE (ancient handbook)
mappings.basis: MIT conventionally gives 135 CE; SEP identifies Arrian’s abridgment of the Discourses.
mappings.note: Approximate archive convention, not securely dated publication; modern Crossley anthology is distinct.

mappings.label: 3rd–2nd century BCE (posthumous compilation)
mappings.basis: Eno argues anonymous texts reflecting third-century thought, plausibly Qin or early Han; broad century bounds avoid false precision.
mappings.note: Anonymous later compilations; preserving attribution does not confirm Confucius wrote these works. Individual sayings may be earlier.

mappings.label: c. 450–250 BCE (text formation)
mappings.basis: SEP describes writing from the later fifth century, fourth-century consolidation, relative stability by mid-third century BCE.
mappings.note: Text formation, not traditional Laozi lifetime. English translations and paraphrases have separate dates.

mappings.label: c. 380–360 BCE
mappings.basis: IEP groups Republic II–X and Symposium here; chronology remains reconstructed.
mappings.note: Observed Republic citation 586a–b is Book IX. Republic Book I belongs to an earlier group if encountered later.

mappings.label: c. 360–355 BCE (proposed chronology)
mappings.basis: IEP proposes this late-transitional group; not scholarly consensus.

mappings.label: c. 369–355 BCE
mappings.basis: Dedicated IEP entry suggests shortly after 369–367; general IEP chronology gives 360–355. Envelope retains disagreement.

mappings.label: c. 355–347 BCE (proposed chronology)
mappings.basis: IEP places Timaeus among late dialogues in this proposed group.
mappings.note: Cited 1888 Archer-Hind edition is not ancient composition.

mappings.label: c. 399–387 BCE
mappings.basis: IEP places this after Socrates’s death and before Plato’s 387 BCE Sicily trip.

mappings.label: c. 350–330 BCE
mappings.basis: Notre Dame gives c. 350; Cambridge list uses c. 330 BCE. Range retains variation.

mappings.label: c. 350 BCE
mappings.basis: Routledge bibliography says mid-fourth century; MIT conventionally gives 350 BCE.
mappings.note: Approximate convention for a layered treatise, not a securely dated single publication.

mappings.label: 458 BCE (first performance)
mappings.basis: Cambridge chronology records the trilogy’s production and first prize in 458 BCE.

mappings.label: 414 BCE (first performance)
mappings.basis: Johnston’s university-hosted historical note gives first production in 414 BCE.

mappings.label: 423 BCE (first performance; text revised later)
mappings.basis: Johnston dates first production to 423 BCE; surviving text is an unfinished later revision.
mappings.note: 423 BCE dates initial production, not every surviving line or the later revision.

mappings.label: 1859 (first publication)
mappings.basis: Freeman’s bibliography identifies the 1859 first edition and 24 November publication.
observedContexts: On the Origin of Species, first edition

mappings.label: 1841 (first publication)
mappings.basis: Harvard’s primary-reading chronology identifies Self-Reliance (1841).

mappings.label: 1651 (first publication)
mappings.basis: British Library preserves the 1651 witness and identifies the 1651 printed edition.

mappings.label: 1913 (first publication; source date corrected)
mappings.basis: AFI explicitly identifies the 1913 novel; corpus title date 1912 is erroneous.
mappings.note: Manual erratum: source year 1912 must not be promoted unchanged.

mappings.label: c. 380–360 BCE (Plato’s Phaedo composition)
mappings.basis: IEP places Phaedo in its proposed middle-period composition group. Socrates is the represented speaker, not the work’s writer.
mappings.note: Dates composition of Plato’s dialogue, not its dramatic setting at Socrates’s death in 399 BCE. Retain the record’s existing speaker attribution.

mappings.label: c. 399–387 BCE (Plato’s Apology composition)
mappings.basis: IEP places Plato’s Apology among early dialogues composed after Socrates’s death and before the 387 BCE Sicily trip.
mappings.note: 399 BCE is the trial/dramatic setting, not an asserted exact composition year. Require explicit Plato context to distinguish Xenophon’s Apology.
